Article Title: 'Largely irrelevant': Jaishankar says UN failing on Gulf, Ukraine, Africa and Covid
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar has called the United Nations “largely irrelevant” to decision-making on major global crises, blaming a “gridlocked” Security Council and its outdated composition for the organisation’s ineffectiveness.Speaking at the fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi on Monday, Jaishankar said the UN had struggled to play a meaningful role in addressing major international issues, including conflicts in the Gulf and Ukraine, crises in Africa and the Covid-19 pandemic.“Where the UN is concerned, I think it's obvious to everybody by now that the UN is gridlocked,” Jaishankar said.“If you look at the big issues of the day... actually, the United Nations has been largely irrelevant to the decision-making,” he added.Jaishankar said much of the problem stemmed from the Security Council’s inability to reach decisions. He also questioned whether its current composition reflected the wider international community.The UN was founded with 51 members and now has almost four times that number, he noted.“So, if you have grown four times, and you want to keep the old board of management, it's not going to work. I mean, it's common sense,” he said.Jaishankar also criticised countries that he said were resisting UN reform while citing Africa’s interests as a reason.He said Africa had already presented a clear position during intergovernmental negotiations on what it wanted from reform of the world body.Despite his criticism, Jaishankar said the answer was not to bypass the UN.“We need the UN. The UN has done a big service to the international community,” he said.“Our job must be to ‘fix the UN, not to work around the UN’,” he added, saying the UN itself needed to contribute to the reform process.India has been pushing for comprehensive UN reforms, including expansion of the Security Council. It has worked with the G4 grouping of India, Japan, Brazil and Germany, as well as the L.69 group of developing countries, to build support for reform.Jaishankar has previously criticised the UN’s structure, saying the organisation had failed to keep pace with a world that had become more interconnected and multipolar.
Article Summary: S Jaishankar says the UN has struggled to play a meaningful role in addressing major international issues. He blames a “gridlocked” Security Council and its outdated composition for the organisation’s ineffectiveness. India has been pushing for comprehensive UN reforms, including expansion of Security Council.

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage claimed gold with 88.55m.Sreeshankar also won silver in the men's long jump with 8.07m despite an injury forcing him to abandon his final two attempts. China's Yuhao Shi took gold with 8.17m.Gulveer added his second silver of the Games with a personal best of 3:36.72 in the men's 1500m, having earlier finished runner-up in the 10,000m.Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5000m with 15:14.61, adding to the bronze she had claimed in the 3000m steeplechase.Vithya Ramraj also took bronze in the women's 400m hurdles with a personal best of 54.75 seconds.Esha Singh secured silver in the women's 25m pistol after finishing with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won the gold after the shoot-off.Pincky Balhara added bronze in the women's -78kg kurash category, losing 0-5 to South Korea's Sumin Mo in the semifinals.Despite the eight medals, India's gold tally remained at four, a crucial factor in the standings as countries are ranked by gold medals first.China led with 132 golds, followed by Japan with 41, South Korea with 21 and Uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.
Article Summary: India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze. The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh.

NEW DELHI: BJP national spokesperson Sambit Patra on Tuesday accused Rahul Gandhi of misleading the public over Form 6. He alleged that the Congress and INDIA bloc were attempting to undermine constitutional institutions amid their planned protest against the Election Commission .Patra said the Supreme Court had not declared Form 6 illegal and had only agreed to examine allegations concerning changes to the form. He also rejected Gandhi's claim of differences within the Election Commission over the issue, citing an ECI fact-check that said the Bihar SIR order was approved unanimously."Rahul Gandhi posted today regarding Form 6 after the hearing in the Supreme Court on the PIL. This is an attack on the Election Commission, but the second line mentions the BJP as well, so the BJP will respond to it. Rahul Gandhi has misled the public on two points," Patra said."First, he claimed that Form 6 was illegal and specifically mentioned the Bharatiya Janata Party in this context. But the court did not declare Form 6 illegal today. The court noted that the petition mentioned changes to Form 6, so the court said it would examine the matter. We had not consented to any such changes. If any change has indeed been made, it will only become clear after the notice is issued," he said."Even after that, when we read the detailed order and look at the Election Commission's press release... it becomes clear that the Commission had explicitly stated that there was no change in Form 6, and the Supreme Court had upheld the associated declaration. Therefore, there is no ambiguity here. When Rahul Gandhi claims that Form 6 was illegal and that the Supreme Court said so today, he is lying," Patra added.Patra also hit out at the Congress and INDIA bloc over their planned march to the Election Commission, alleging that the opposition was seeking to weaken democratic institutions to facilitate Gandhi's political rise."A sponsored attempt is being made by opposition parties, especially the Congress, as to how a change of power can be brought about in the country and Rahul Gandhi be made to sit in power just like that. For this, a blow to India's democracy and constitutional bodies is being hurled in a sponsored manner," he said."After failing multiple times, Congress leaders decided to establish anarchy in the country and attack institutions... Today again, they are trying to create anarchy and undermine democratic institutions by allegedly marching towards the Election Commission," Patra said.He alleged that the Congress had been attempting for years to "launch and relaunch Rahul Gandhi", and accused the opposition of attacking institutions after failing to do so through electoral politics.On the alleged dissent within the poll panel, Patra said the Election Commission had clarified that its order on the Special Intensive Revision in Bihar was issued with the unanimous approval of all commissioners."The fact-check states that the order regarding SIR in Bihar was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission. Subsequently, the Supreme Court of India upheld this order in its decision. It was indeed a unanimous decision with no room for doubt," he said.
Article Summary: BJP national spokesperson Sambit Patra accused Rahul Gandhi of misleading the public over Form 6. He alleged that the Congress and INDIA bloc were attempting to undermine constitutional institutions amid their planned protest against the Election Commission. Patra said the Supreme Court had not declared Form 6 illegal and had only agreed to examine allegations concerning changes to the form.

Article Title: 'Beyond limits': Ex-CJI Gavai, former judges slam SC judge Ujjal Bhuyan's remarks amid EC-SIR row
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai and other retired judges on Monday condemned Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan's remarks on the Election Commission.Gavai said that a sitting judge should not have made comments on the ongoing row over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls as the matter is sub judice before the top court."Judicial propriety would not permit him to make any comment on the matter which is sub judice before the court," Gavai told news agency PTI.Retired Delhi high court judges SN Dhingra and RS Sodhi also questioned Bhuyan's remarks.Justice Dhingra said Bhuyan's statement was "way beyond the limits of a sitting top court judge" and such comments should not be made at a public event when the issue is pending before the same court."He should have thought a thousand times before making such a statement," Dhingra said, adding that Justice Bhuyan did not know the full facts of the issue.Justice R S Sodhi also criticised Justice Bhuyan for calling the SIR exercise disenfranchisement and said that the right to vote was governed by the statutory framework."Whether you have a vote or you don't have a vote depends upon the statute. If you fall within the parameters of the statute, you have a vote.If you don't fall within the parameters of the statute, you don't have a vote," Justice Sodhi said."I mean, these hardline thinking and these hardline statements, to my mind, are not a very mature way of looking at a thing, especially when you are supposed to be in a field which is supposed to be excellent in its rationalising," he said.This comes a day after Justice Bhuyan said that any process that "disenfranchises" millions of Indian citizens was "intrinsically arbitrary" and a "negation" of the constitutional order.While delivering the valedictory address at the 19th Justice Bodh Raj Sawhney Memorial Moot Court Competition at NALSAR University of Law on Sunday, Justice Bhuyan said that the Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens, one with voting rights and the other without voting rights, and no amount of "whataboutery" could justify such a process.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary. No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution and I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution of India,” Bar and Bench quoted Justice Bhuyan as saying.He said the Constitution does not create two classes of citizens based on voting rights and added that wholesale disenfranchisement would violate Articles 326 and 14.“No authority can do it; no court can condone it. No one is above the Constitution,” he said.This is not the first time that Justice Bhuyan has put forth his views on issues being discussed in the public domain.Recently, NALSAR Hyderabad was in the news after a section of its students wrote to the vice chancellor, registrar and professors of the institution, opposing any proposal to invite Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as chief guest to the varsity's convocation.Justice Bhuyan, who served as the Chancellor of NALSAR, on Sunday said he can be legitimately proud of the students of the institution."You have shown to the country and the world what a university student, that too, a student of law, should be like. You are brilliant. You are bold and you are brave," he said.
Article Summary: Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai and other retired judges on Monday condemned Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan's remarks on the Election Commission. Justice Dhingra and RS Sodhi said Bhuya's statement was "way beyond the limits of a sitting top court judge" This comes a day after Justice Bhuayan said that any process that "disenfranchises" millions of Indian citizens was "intrinsically arbitrary"

NEW DELHI: Chirag Paswan once described himself as Prime Minister Narendra Modi's "Hanuman". Six years later, the LJP (Ram Vilas) chief offered another approach of his politics: "I can stand up to my government . .. I am in the alliance but I am not the BJP."This distinction becomes relevant as he prepares to take his party into the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly election. LJP(RV) has announced that it will contest the polls and is preparing for all 403 constituencies, while leaving open whether it will eventually contest alone or as part of an alliance.The UP move comes after a significant change in Chirag Paswan's political position. In 2020, the undivided LJP broke with the NDA in Bihar, contested 135 seats and targeted Nitish Kumar's JD(U), while maintaining its support for PM Modi. Its slogan captured the strategy: "Modi se bair nahi, Nitish teri khair nahi." The party won only one seat, but its 5.66% vote share had a measurable impact on the results.Since then, LJP(RV) has moved from being a marginal alliance partner to a more consequential NDA component.It won all five Lok Sabha seats it contested in Bihar in 2024, giving Chirag Paswan a 100% strike rate, and in the 2025 assembly election it contested 29 seats under the NDA arrangement and won 19. The BJP and JD(U) contested 101 seats each, while LJP(RV) secured 29.That progression provides the context for the 403-seat announcement. Chirag Paswan now has five Lok Sabha MPs, 19 MLAs in Bihar and a Union cabinet position. The question is whether that political weight can be extended beyond Bihar.The latest phase of the UP push took shape in September, when Paswan launched his party's youth outreach in Prayagraj. At the "Youth Bole Toh" programme, he spoke about education, employment, skills and greater youth participation in politics, and announced plans for a National Youth Commission.On September 28, he made the electoral plan explicit: "There is no doubt that LJP (Ram Vilas) will contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections."The following day, he said the response in Prayagraj had strengthened his confidence in the UP plan. LJP(RV) MP Rajesh Verma subsequently said the party was preparing for all 403 seats, while making clear that the eventual alliance arrangement would be decided later.The 2020 Bihar assembly election was the debut test of Chirag Paswan's leadership. His father, Ram Vilas Paswan , had just died a few days ago.The LJP won only one seat but emerged as a significant factor in 54 constituencies where its vote total was greater than the victory margin. In 25 seats where JD(U) finished second, LJP's vote exceeded the winning margin. Chirag was explicit about the objective, saying after the election: "My main idea in the election was to make the BJP stronger. I am happy with the impact I have had in this election."The BJP finished with 74 seats in that election, ahead of JD(U)'s 43 for the first time. The episode demonstrated that LJP did not need to win seats itself to affect the relative strength of its larger alliance partner.The 2025 Bihar election showed the other side of the equation. LJP(RV) was no longer operating as a spoiler outside the alliance. It contested 29 seats as an NDA partner and won 19, converting its electoral relevance into representation inside the alliance.UP could now test both models: LJP(RV) as an alliance partner with an electoral base of its own, and LJP(RV) as a potential vote-splitter in constituencies where even a few thousand votes can decide the outcome.The potential constituency is significant, but far from straightforward.The BSP won no seats in the 2024 Lok Sabha election in UP and polled around 9.4%. At the same time, the SP expanded its support among Dalit voters as part of its broader PDA coalition. A Lokniti-CSDS post-poll analysis showed a sharp difference between Jatav and non-Jatav Dalit voting patterns, with the BSP retaining much stronger support among Jatavs than among non-Jatav Dalits.For Chirag Paswan, the challenge is therefore larger than taking the Paswan identity from Bihar to UP. Pasis, Valmikis, Khatiks and other non-Jatav communities have distinct political histories and local calculations. Whether LJP(RV) can persuade sections of these voters that it is a credible political vehicle will determine whether its UP expansion produces votes or merely an organisational footprint.The impact could also vary by constituency. A modest LJP(RV) vote could matter in a close BJP-SP contest if it draws disproportionately from one side's potential support base. But unlike Bihar in 2020, there is no single obvious target. The BJP, SP, BSP and Congress have overlapping social coalitions, making the direction of any vote transfer harder to predict.The UP expansion also fits Paswan's attempt to establish LJP(RV) beyond its Bihar base. The party has already demonstrated that it can operate outside the state: in the 2023 Nagaland assembly election, it contested 16 seats, won two and finished runner-up in eight, securing more than 8.6% of the vote.But UP is on a different scale. A credible organisation here would give Chiag Paswan a political presence in the country's largest state and potentially strengthen his position in future NDA negotiations.His recent conduct suggests that maintaining an independent identity is part of that calculation. He has criticised the Bihar government's handling of law and order while remaining part of the NDA, and questioned the Election Commission over concerns surrounding SIR before welcoming its subsequent clarification.The UP experiment, therefore, would not simply be about how many seats LJP(RV) could win. It would be abot whether Chirag Paswan can build an influence outside Bihar to make his party a more consequential NDA partner, while retaining the political independence he summed up in his own words: "I am in the alliance but I am not the BJP."
Article Summary: LJP (Ram Vilas) chief Chirag Paswan is set to contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election. The party is preparing for all 403 seats, while leaving open whether it will eventually contest alone or as part of an alliance.

NEW DELHI: The new Congress team in Uttar Pradesh has a daunting challenge at hand: to revive the fortunes of the grand-old-party in the 2027 assembly elections. But before the big political test early next year, there is a pressing concern at hand: the alliance dynamics. And to that extent, the Congress appointments send a mixed signal to ally Samajwadi Party.The appointment of MLA Aradhana Misra-Mona, who is perceived close to SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, as the new state chief signals the willingness of the Congress for an amicable seat-sharing discussions. But the simultaneous elevation of Imran Masood, a known critic of Samjawadi Party’s “big brother attitude”, raises obvious questions about the Congress’s intent vis-a-vis its ally.So, how will this contradiction play out when the two parties sit on the table to decide the contours of their alliance? More so, as there is already an open war of words between the leaders of the two parties over the seat share. Congress leaders have insisted that division of seats should be based on “respect and equality.” Aradhana Misra-Mona acknowledges that with the 2027 state elections only a few months away, she would have to hit the ground running as her party seeks to regain political space it has steadily lost in the state since 1989.To understand why Imran Masood’s high-profile appointment may have caused some unease, here’s a look at some of the statements he has made in the recent past.In a video on X Imran Masood said thatClearly, very strong statements which have led to equally strong reactions from the Samajwadi Party. Akhilesh has led the pushback for the Samajwadi Party, making it clear that winnability will be the only criteria for division of seats.When asked about Masood’s remarks, Akhilesh once said: “I have nothing to do with the statement given by anyone. Our INDIA alliance is intact. Those who want to leave the INDIA alliance can go.”Amid reports that the Congress was seeking 150 seats, Samajwadi Party MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel said the grand-old-party should seek seats in proportion to its electoral strength and organisational presence in the state."I think if they are given 50 seats, they should look at their actual position and status before seeking anything more than 50 seats. They should look at their past record. I understand that in Uttar Pradesh, there is no mandate for Congress. If they fight with us, they will benefit. They have only two MLAs in the state. If they fight together, they will benefit."Masood and SP leaders have also engaged in open war of words over who, Rahul or Akhilesh, was more capable of leading the fight against the BJP.While a lot of these remarks are posturing for dominance in seat-sharing talks, the fact is that the open fighting between the two allies has the potential to confuse their cadres. The Congress move to give prominence to Masood could be part of its strategy to keep the pressure going on the Samajwadi Party.However, former Congress leader and senior political commentator Sanjay Jha feels Congress and Samajwadi Party are not in competition. He asserts that Masood’s appointment has a much bigger and important messaging for the minorities, something the Congress should have done long ago.“UP has seen a lot of polarisation under the BJP regime. Muslims form 18% of the state’s population. I think Masood’s appointment is a manifestation of Congress actually beginning to do what it should have done a long time ago, to be bold, to embrace the fact that the minorities are vulnerable under the BJP, that the Muslims need representation, and to stand for them by having a representative who is going to be a working president. The message is very clear that we are not scared, we are not fearful of the majority community treating the Congress or the Samajwadi party, as the BJP likes to call it, as the "Miya" party,” says Sanjay Jha.“I think the more the opposition becomes fearless and embraces secularism and stands up for Muslims who have been targeted in a blatant fashion, is good for politics. So I endorse the political standpoint of the Congress,” Sanjay Jha adds.Masood is a first-time MP and a prominent face in western Uttar Pradesh politics. Ahead of the 2022 UP assembly polls, Masood left the Congress and to join the SP. However, left the SP in October that year and joined the BSP, where Mayawati immediately appointed him coordinator for western UP. In August 2023, however, Mayawati expelled Masood from the party, accusing him of indiscipline and “anti-party activities”. NEW DELHI: Women's success rate in JEE-Advanced reached a record high in 2026 despite fewer registrations, with over 10,000 qualifying for the first time during this period. Yet their share of IIT seat allotments barely changed, from 20.15% to 20.22%. Of the top 100 rankers, 97 were allotted seats at just three IITs - Bombay, Delhi and Madras - with Bombay alone taking 68.This time, a total 18,861 admissions were made in IITs, with 20% being female candidates. Among the top 25 rankers, 8 candidates each took admission in IIT Delhi and IIT Madras, while six toppers took admission in IIT Bombay.The Joint Implementation Committee report, prepared by IIT Roorkee, shows sharp gains for SC and ST candidates. Including candidates with disabilities in both years, their qualification rates among registered candidates rose by 9.9 and 8.3 percentage points, respectively, to 50.2% and 42.1%.SC qualifiers increased from 12,528 to 15,856, while the ST count rose from 5,017 to 6,379. Both increases were around 27%, faster than the 4.6% rise in the number of qualifiers, from 54,378 to 56,880.Of 43,112 registered women, 10,107 qualified, taking their success rate to 23.4%, against 21.7% last year.In 2025, 9,404 women qualified from 43,413 registrations. Among women who appeared in both papers, the success rate was 24.9%.Women accounted for 23% of registrations but 17.8% of qualifiers, showing that their improved success rate has yet to close the gap with male candidates.Women received 3,814 seat allotments, up from 3,664, out of 18,861 overall. Their qualifying count grew 7.5%.IITs have added seats exclusively for women to ensure they make up at least one in five new undergraduate students. Their share of allotments is only slightly above that level. The report records 3,777 allotments in seats set aside for women and 37 in seats open to all genders. Women are considered first for women-only seats within the relevant category.The small number allotted seats open to all therefore does not show how many could have secured them on rank alone.The qualifying total also includes students eligible for a one-year preparatory course before starting an IIT degree. Their number rose from 9,644 to 13,127, nearly a quarter of all qualifiers. This route is available to eligible SC and ST candidates and those with disabilities against unfilled reserved seats. Those admitted must pass the course before entering allotted degree programme.Excluding this group, SC and ST qualifiers still increased by about 17% and 19%. However, the overall number qualifying directly for degree programmes fell from 44,734 to 43,753. The report records 189 seat allotments for this course. Qualifying for either of these routes does not guarantee an IIT seat; admission also depends on rank, eligibility and available seats.
Article Summary: Of 43,112 registered women, 10,107 qualified, taking their success rate to 23.4%. In 2025, 9,404 women qualified from 43,413 registrations. Women received 3,814 seat allotments, up from 3,664, out of 18,861 overall.

NEW DELHI: Taking note of safety concerns emerging from across states the National Commission for Women has issued guidelines to states and UTs for safety of women passengers using app-based and digital transport services calling for appropriate verification of criminal antecedents, police verification and background of drivers before onboarding, monitoring of drivers operating during late-night hours and providing SOS buttons in every cab to send out alerts to the command-and-control centre.The NCW notes that as cabs, auto-rickshaws, bike taxis and other app-enabled transport services have become an integral part of everyday mobility, particularly for women travelling independently, ensuring safety throughout the journey has assumed greater importance.Instances relating to mismatch in driver or vehicle identity, route deviation, inappropriate conduct, harassment, stalking, unsafe drop-offs, delays in emergency response and inadequate grievance redressal underline the need for a coordinated and accountable safety framework.The guidelines issued in this backdrop also take into consideration the recommendations of the Justice J S Verma Committee Report, 2013, and the regulatory framework under the Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines, 2025, issued by the ministry of road transport and highways.NCW chairperosn Vijaya Rahatkar, has written to the chief secretaries of all states and UTs, requesting appropriate measures for implementation of the guidelines.Bringing focus on verification of driver and vehicle, the guidelines lay down that the aggregators shall ensure that the driver and vehicle assigned to a passenger match the details displayed on the application. “Any unauthorised change in the driver or vehicle shall be appropriately flagged in the application and treated as a safety concern,” it asserts. The guidelines also call for mechanisms for real-time alerts for route deviations or suspicious stoppages.The guidelines also call for penalty-free cancellation in case of identity mismatch. The guidelines also lay down that the aggregators must strive to maintain a verified pool of women drivers, enabling women travelling alone with the option to request a woman driver through the application.Calling for enhanced verification and monitoring of drivers operating during late-night hours, the guidelines set out measures ranging from mandatory driver photo verification at trip commencement, addressing driver intoxication, enhanced command and control centre monitoring and a safe-drop option at the end of the ride.“Aggregators may establish a dedicated and time-bound grievance redressal mechanism for complaints relating to driver misconduct, harassment, assault, route deviation, unauthorised driver or vehicle substitution and failure of emergency-response mechanisms,” the guidelines state.
Article Summary: The National Commission for Women issued guidelines to states and UTs for safety of women passengers using app-based and digital transport services. The guidelines call for appropriate verification of criminal antecedents, police verification and background of drivers before onboarding, monitoring of drivers operating during late-night hours and providing SOS buttons in every cab.

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”

Article Title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan

NEW DELHI: Launching a scathing attack on special intensive revision (SIR) that has resulted in large-scale deletion of names from voter lists across states, Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution.Discounting the reasons given by govt and EC to justify SIR, which was upheld in the case of the revision of rolls in West Bengal by SC with modifications, Justice Bhuyan said, "No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of Constitution. I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution."He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad.Nalsar students, who had opposed CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation ceremony recently, came in for praise from Justice Bhuyan.Also read| Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman "One last word about the brilliant students of Nalsar. You have shown to the country and to the world what a university student, that too a student of law, should be. You are brilliant, you are bold, and you are brave," he said.Justice Bhuyan said a citizen’s right to vote was central to the holding of free and fair elections.“Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing,” he added.The SC judge said the right to vote or be included in the voters’ list could not be detached from the persona of an Indian citizen.Also read: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added. Justice Bhuyan said the Indian Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens: citizens with voting rights and citizens without voting rights. “Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution of India,” he said.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary,” he added, his remarks coinciding with attacks on EC and govt over SIR by the opposition and others.Justice Bhuyan said the right to vote was intertwined with India’s years of struggle against foreign rule. “It is a manifestation of our freedom achieved after so much struggle and sacrifice. Article 326 (universal adult franchise) cannot be tinkered with at all. No authority can do it, no court can condone it. No one is above Constitution,” he said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution. He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad. “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added.

Article Title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35M Ohio mansion has a $1.75M architectural twin in Illinois
Article Text:
Travis Kelce (Image via Getty)

Travis Kelce’s Ohio mansion has a historic architectural connection

The House of Seven Gables in Wheaton, Illinois, was built in 1897.Blank Creative

House of Seven Gables offers a smaller version of Kelce’s mansion

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Travis Kelce’s new Ohio mansion has an unusual connection to another historic home nearly 400 miles away. The Kansas City Chiefs star paid $5.35 million for Moyenage, a grand estate overlooking Lake Erie, but its history stretches beyond football and celebrity real estate. The mansion was designed for the same steel magnate who commissioned a strikingly similar house in Illinois several years earlier. Now, that architectural relative, the House of Seven Gables in Wheaton, is on the market for $1.75 million, offering buyers a rare chance to own a piece of the story behind Kelce’s impressive new property.Kelce’s Bratenahl estate, known as Moyenage, stands out for its scale. The roughly 21,000-square-foot property sits on 3.5 acres overlooking Lake Erie and includes eight bedrooms, a game room, home theatre and a separate two-bedroom gatehouse.But the story behind the house makes the property even more intriguing.Architect Jarvis Hunt originally designed Moyenage for Chicago steel magnate Jay C. Morse around the start of the 20th century. Before that, Hunt had designed the House of Seven Gables in Wheaton, Illinois, for Morse in 1897.Jenny Ames of Engel & Völkers Chicago, who is representing the Illinois property with Lisa Grimes, said the connection is more than a coincidence.“The resemblance is really quite remarkable,”“Historical accounts indicate that when Morse later built Moyenage in Ohio, he asked Hunt to design it based on his Wheaton home,” Ames said. “So when you look at the two houses side by side, you are not simply seeing two homes by the same architect. You are seeing two versions of a very personal architectural vision created for the same owner.”Both properties showcase Tudor and Jacobean influences, with brick exteriors, steep gables, large chimneys and elaborate interiors.The Illinois home is considerably smaller than Kelce’s Ohio residence, covering about 10,000 square feet on less than half an acre. It has seven bedrooms, three floors and a newly built three-car garage.Inside, however, its historic character remains strong. Original fireplaces, oak panelling, carved woodwork, flooring, leaded glass and beamed ceilings have survived decades of changes.“The interiors are where the relationship becomes especially interesting,” Ames said. “Both homes have extraordinary woodwork, beamed ceilings, substantial staircases, leaded glass and formal rooms organized on a grand scale.”The property also has an unusual survival story. After serving as the Loretto Convent for decades, the mansion faced demolition during redevelopment. In 2017, workers moved the approximately 730-ton structure about 500 feet to a new site.“They moved the structure intact,” Ames said.The remarkable operation involved placing the mansion on steel beams and 21 hydraulic dollies before moving it onto a new foundation. The process reportedly took about six hours.For Kelce, Moyenage is now part of his growing real estate portfolio. For prospective buyers in Illinois, the House of Seven Gables offers something even more unusual: a chance to own the architectural predecessor of the Chiefs star’s historic Ohio retreat.
Article Summary: Travis Kelce’s new Ohio mansion has an unusual connection to another historic home nearly 400 miles away. The Kansas City Chiefs star paid $5.35 million for Moyenage, a grand estate overlooking Lake Erie. The mansion was designed for the same steel magnate who commissioned a strikingly similar house in Illinois several years earlier.

Article Title: Travis Kelce-backed Six Flags gets major green upgrade with 20.8 million kWh solar project amid lawsuits

Six Flags Magic Mountain solar project now powers two parks

Travis Kelce’s Six Flags endorsement adds another spotlight

A theme park parking lot is usually a place where cars sit before the real fun begins. At Six Flags Magic Mountain in California, it now plays a much bigger role. The park has fully activated a major solar power project covering thousands of parking spaces, turning an everyday guest facility into a large-scale energy source. The installation is designed to generate enough electricity to offset the annual consumption of both Six Flags Magic Mountain and neighbouring Hurricane Harbor Los Angeles. The move also arrives as NFL star Travis Kelce continues his high-profile relationship with Six Flags as the company’s brand ambassador.The newly energised project includes solar canopies covering 4,315 parking spaces, giving the Magic Mountain parking area a striking new purpose. The system has a 12.37-megawatt solar capacity, making it the largest solar carport installation in California, according to project information.The solar installation is expected to produce around 20.8 million kWh of electricity each year. Six Flags says that output is equivalent to the annual electricity consumption of Magic Mountain and Hurricane Harbor Los Angeles combined.The project also features an 8 MWh battery energy storage system and 109 electric vehicle charging stations.That means the development is not simply about putting solar panels above cars. It combines power generation, energy storage and EV infrastructure in one large site.The project had been announced earlier, but its full commissioning marks the key milestone. The solar canopies cover roughly 637,000 square feet, with 22,908 solar modules spread across 36 long-span carport structures.The message shown in the accompanying Parks & Loisirs post sums up the scale of the development: “Le parking de Six Flags Magic Mountain alimente désormais deux parcs en énergie solaire.” Translated, it means the Six Flags Magic Mountain parking lot now supplies solar energy to two parks.The image also states that the 12.37 MW installation covers 4,315 parking spaces and that its yearly production should match the combined electricity consumption of Magic Mountain and Hurricane Harbor Los Angeles.The sustainability push comes during a major branding chapter for Six Flags. In March 2026, the company announced Travis Kelce as a brand ambassador for 2026. His role includes digital content, social media campaigns and approved use of his name, image and likeness across broadcast, streaming and in-park marketing.Kelce has also described himself as a lifelong Six Flags fan. In the company's announcement, he said:“Six Flags parks were a hallmark of my childhood and the scene of some of my most fun and cherished memories, and I’m excited to team up with the company as it enters its next chapter. The Six Flags team is creating even more rides and attractions as it takes guest engagement to a new level. I look forward to helping them continue to build excitement for their unrivaled portfolio of parks and introduce a new generation of fans to unforgettable experiences. ”His endorsement gives Six Flags a familiar sports personality while the company makes changes beyond rides and attractions. At Magic Mountain, the parking lot itself has become part of that next chapter, producing renewable energy on a scale capable of supporting two major Southern California parks.
Article Summary: Six Flags Magic Mountain has fully activated a major solar power project. The installation is designed to generate enough electricity to offset the annual consumption of both parks. The move also arrives as NFL star Travis Kelce continues his high-profile relationship with Six Flags as the company’s brand ambassador.

Earlier this year, Travis and Jason Kelce made a quiet contribution that helped make a special Olympic moment possible for U.S. hockey star Laila Edwards. The brothers donated $10,000 to a fundraiser that helped bring Edwards’ family and friends to Milan for the 2026 Winter Olympics. Their support came after her family faced a difficult choice between watching her Olympic debut and covering everyday household expenses. Edwards went on to help Team USA win gold, creating a moment her family could celebrate together.Edwards’ Olympic journey was already historic before she stepped onto the ice. The 22-year-old became the first Black American to win an Olympic medal in women’s ice hockey after Team USA defeated Canada in the gold-medal game.But getting her loved ones to Italy was not easy.Edwards’ father, Robert Edwards, launched a GoFundMe campaign titled “Send Laila’s Family to the Olympics to Cheer Her On!” with a $50,000 target. The goal was designed to help the family avoid choosing between Olympic travel and essential bills at home in Cleveland Heights, Ohio.The Kelce brothers, who also grew up in Cleveland Heights, had followed Edwards’ career since she became the first Black player to make the U.S.senior women’s national team in 2023. They later supported her through an anonymous $10,000 donation.The contribution helped make the trip possible for 14 people, including Edwards’ parents, grandmother, aunt, cousin and older brother.The family had initially been able to afford travel for only two people.“We had to start talking about how to get money,” her mother Charone Gray-Edwards said, according to the Associated Press. “Who would go? How would we afford it?”The Chiefs tight end’s support extended beyond the financial contribution. Travis also reached out to Edwards before her Olympic debut, offering encouragement as she prepared for the biggest stage of her young career.“He was just saying, everyone’s got my back. He’s rooting for me,” she said, per the AP. “They didn’t have to do that, but they did. And I’m really grateful.”Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie, were also in the stands for the gold-medal game, giving Edwards a familiar connection to her hometown while she represented the United States.Edwards made an impact on the ice, recording an assist during the gold-medal victory. Her family had made the long journey to Milan, and the Kelce brothers had quietly helped make that possible. Their involvement added another meaningful layer to an already historic Olympic chapter.

Article Title: 86 to 101: Virat Kohli's final ODI window to break Sachin Tendulkar's century record
Article Text:
Virat Kohli's final ODI window to break Sachin Tendulkar's century record

86 to 101: The century equation begins

India or overseas? The recent pattern in Kohli's centuries

2027 World Cup: Kohli's final shot at Sachin's record

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Only ODI cricket remains

It was the semi-final of the 2023 World Cup when Virat Kohli scored his 50th ODI century in front of Sachin Tendulkar, surpassing his idol's record of 49 hundreds in the format. That innings put another Tendulkar record within Kohli's reach. Tendulkar's 100 international centuries remain the benchmark, leaving Kohli with a chance to become the first batter to reach 101.But the equation changed when Kohli retired from Test cricket on May 12, 2025. With his T20I career already over, ODI cricket became his only remaining route to Tendulkar's record. Now, with the 2027 World Cup less than a year away, Kohli has 86 international centuries - 14 short of equalling Tendulkar and 15 away from surpassing him.His latest hundred, a 139 not out against West Indies in the first ODI of the recently concluded series, was followed by 29 in the second match and a golden duck in the third.So how many opportunities does Kohli have left, and can he turn them into the 15 centuries he needs to move past Tendulkar's 100?India currently have 11 confirmed bilateral ODIs scheduled before the 2027 World Cup - five against New Zealand, three against Sri Lanka and three against Zimbabwe.India's World Cup campaign will begin against Australia in Cape Town on October 7, 2027.The new FTP could add another six-match ODI series in South Africa in the weeks before the World Cup, giving India a chance to acclimatise to conditions ahead of the tournament. However, that series is not part of the confirmed schedule as of yet.The Asia Cup is another part of the picture. The 2027 tournament is scheduled to be played in Bangladesh from June 18 to July 4 and is expected to return to the ODI format. A detailed fixture list has not been announced, but based on the 2023 format, India could play up to six matches if they reach the final.The World Cup itself will have five group-stage matches and if the team reaches the Super 7, they will play six more matches, with a semi-final and final to follow if they go all the way. A finalist could therefore play a maximum of 13 matches at the tournament.That leaves Kohli with 11 confirmed bilateral ODIs before the World Cup, with the Asia Cup providing additional opportunities before the tournament.For Kohli, the target remains 15 centuries.Kohli's recent ODI numbers are markedly different at home and overseas. In his last 32 ODI matches in India, he has scored nine centuries. In his last 32 overseas ODIs, he has scored three - in Dubai, Chattogram and Colombo.That split comes into focus with India scheduled to play five ODIs in New Zealand before the World Cup.Kohli's overall record overseas, though, is substantial. He has scored 27 of his 55 ODI centuries outside India. Bangladesh is his most productive overseas country, with six centuries, followed by Sri Lanka and Australia with five each. He has four in the West Indies, three in South Africa and one each in New Zealand, England, Zimbabwe and the UAE.Sri Lanka remains one of Kohli's most productive opponents. Kohli has scored 10 ODI centuries against Sri Lanka, his highest tally against any opponent. The three-match series in December will be played in India, with the ODIs scheduled for December 13, 16 and 19. Zimbabwe follow with three matches on January 3, 6 and 9.Kohli's World Cup record gives him a strong base to build on. In 37 World Cup matches, he has scored 1,795 runs at an average of 59.83, with five centuries and 12 half-centuries.The 2023 edition was his most productive World Cup. He scored 765 runs, including three centuries and six half-centuries, and finished as the tournament's leading run-scorer. It was also the tournament in which he scored his 50th ODI century, moving past Tendulkar's record of 49.Kohli has already crossed 15000 ODI runs, becoming only the second batter after Tendulkar to reach the mark. He did so in his 303rd innings. With Test and T20I cricket behind him, every international century Kohli scores from here will come in ODIs. He has also said that the 2027 World Cup will be his last World Cup for India.Fifteen hundreds remain between Kohli and 101.
Article Summary: Virat Kohli has scored 86 ODI centuries - 14 short of Sachin Tendulkar's record. The 2027 World Cup is less than a year away and Kohli's last chance to break the record. India have 11 confirmed bilateral ODIs before the World Cup. The Asia Cup is expected to return to the ODI format.

Article Title: LeBron James’ wife Savannah James’ latest flight incident offers an important rich-people financial lesson as the internet argues over dopamine-hitting morality
Article Text:
Savannah James and her bestie, April McDaniel. Image via: JC Olivera/Variety via Getty Images

Savannah James and April McDaniel on their flight arrangement

Critics and defenders split over the seat gap

Savannah and McDaniel respond to the backlash

The money lesson inside the seat split

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

It’s not easy to be rich. While LeBron James has built his massive financial empire from his career earnings, several business ventures, and endorsements, his wife, Savannah James, is slowly climbing the ladder to create her own financial empire. Recently, news of Savannah and her best friend, April McDaniel, broke online. Fans were quite upset, most of them anyway, and the reason for their big upset was that dopamine-hitting morality was missing from the picture. The two laid out the arrangement on the Sept. 28 episode of Boardroom's Mental Wealth podcast, and the clip has been fought over online ever since.But that was the point, McDaniel was not upset, and her account secretly revealed an important lesson. Let’s have a look at what happened first and how their reactions to the incident gave away a subtle message about money.The hosts, Rich Kleiman and Jack Howard, opened with a broad question about how friendship and money mix, and the exchange came about four minutes into the episode. McDaniel answered first. She said the two live different lifestyles and neither pretends otherwise.It shows in how they travel. McDaniel can't take a spontaneous trip, so the pair book well ahead, which keeps costs down, and James leaves enough time for McDaniel to get her finances lined up.They don't turn up at Fashion Week on a week's notice, whatever people assume about how they move. On a recent trip, reportedly to Japan according to local media, James took first class and McDaniel took business. First was outside what McDaniel planned to spend, and she saw no reason to match James seat for seat. They laugh about it, she said.The two are not casual travel companions. They have been friends for well over a decade, and McDaniel described the move into business together as organic. They co-host the podcast Everybody's Crazy and run a holding company called Signed, and James owns the skincare brand, Reframe Beauty. McDaniel also runs a creative agency.The seat split had come up on their own show before the Mental Wealth appearance, McDaniel said, and some viewers were openly critical. One detail seemed to bother people most. During flights, she goes up front, gets into James' bed and watches a movie with her. “And I was like: ‘Why? I can't afford first,'” April said.The hosts then asked James whether friends had ever expected her to cover a first-class seat for them.Celebrity Net Worth puts Savannah's wealth near $100 million.Critics started with cost. A $10,000 fare is very negligible for Savannah. Others said withholding an upgrade felt like a quiet reminder that the two women are not on the same level. A few wanted James to either buy the ticket or sit in economy with her friend. Some asked why anyone would sit alone on a long flight just to prove a point.Paying with points does not make the seat free, since taxes and fees still have to be paid in cash and can run into the thousands.Commenters argued that paying once invites more, first the spa day and then the dinner check. Boundaries, in this view, are what let a friendship survive a wealth gap, and handouts can breed resentment or entitlement. Praise went to McDaniel for staying within her means and to James for not letting friends become moochers.Former Knicks star Brandon Jennings sided with them on X. His post, from @Tuff__Crowd: "If you can't afford first class or certain things when you around your rich friends and you feel entitled that they should pay, Ur a certified moocher…Savannah James ain't wrong."McDaniel called it ridiculous to assume everybody should fly first and said expectations need managing. She described a recent run-in with someone stunned that she flies commercial instead of private, and she played it for laughs by asking the person if they were okay. In her view, social media has bent people's sense of what things cost, and people used to fast money treat it differently than people who earn it slowly. She wants others to know it is fine to live a normal life.Her rule for money is to worry about yourself. The two live in separate worlds, she said, and meet up to talk about them. She credits James with adjusting to where she is financially, and says the friendship runs on feel. If a plan doesn't feel good to both of them, they skip it.James spoke to the other half of the question. Her friends, she said, understand the situation before any trip begins, and every one of them respects it. Nobody has asked her to take care of a cost or be responsible for them. It "has never, ever been that," she said. She voiced gratitude for that understanding.McDaniel stressed that the friendship holds because each side respects the other's finances.On the podcast, two women with very different bank balances said out loud what each can spend, and neither apologized for her number. They didn’t have to.Howard, who leads money wellness at Ally and has taught budgeting for 16 years, shared that she believes a bank account should show a person's values, and for most people it doesn't. She opens with a question about a person's first memory of money, because she sees two common mistakes, people don't know their money story, and they don't know what they value now. Neither is a math problem. Shame does more damage than arithmetic. Someone who can't afford brunch puts it on a card instead of saying so. Her fix is one honest sentence that offers a cheaper plan, because once it is said, "shame loses its power."James described her own version. Her tax bracket and the prices around her have changed, she said, but her view of what things are worth has not. Spending that follows values makes the seat choice easy for both women: McDaniel pays for what fits her plan, and James pays for what fits hers.Of course, the higher earner does not have to match a friend's standard of living, and saying what each person can afford keeps the relationship steady. Experts also advise telling friends honestly how much you can spend before signing up for travel or dinners.Howard offers a practical start for anyone with uneven income. Fold a sheet of paper into three columns and log every expense, the emotion behind it and the value it served. Do it for 30 days, then build next year's budget from what the log shows.
Article Summary: Savannah James and her best friend, April McDaniel, sat together in first class on a recent flight to Japan. The two were on Boardroom's Mental Wealth podcast, and the clip has been fought over online ever since. McDaniel was not upset, and her account secretly revealed an important lesson. The money lesson inside the seat split is that money is not everything.

Today, I step down as captain of the Indian Women’s Cricket Team across all formats.

I have seen it all.

I have seen the lowest moments, the heartbreak, the criticism, the doubts and the days when nothing seemed to go our way.

NEW DELHI: Lovlina Borgohain ’s Asian Games gold was not just a medal upgrade from silver in the last edition. It was the latest marker in a 15-year career that has taken the Assam boxer through Olympic success, injuries, difficult phases and a mentally demanding Paris 2024 campaign.At the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Borgohain finally changed the colour of her Asian Games medal, defeating China’s Bao Ziyi 5-0 in the women’s 75kg final. The victory, on her 29th birthday, made her only the second Indian woman after MC Mary Kom to win boxing gold at the Asian Games -- 12 years after Kom’s 2014 triumph.For Borgohain, however, the gold's significance went beyond the history books.“It’s still difficult to get out of this moment. I still have the gold medal in my hand," said a beaming Borgohain while lifting the gold medal next to her face. "It’s a very special moment for me. I can’t express how I feel,” she continued as she spoke to TimesofIndia.com upon returning from Japan.Borgohain had finished with silver at the 2022 Hangzhou Asian Games, losing to China’s Li Qian in the final. Three years later, she returned to the continental stage determined to go one step further.Her path to the gold in Nagoya was not straightforward. She began with a 5-0 quarter-final win over South Korea’s Seong Su-yeon before edging Kazakhstan’s reigning 70kg world champion Natalya Bogdanova 3-2 in a closely fought semi-final.She then produced a 5-0 win over Ziyi in the final.The contrast with Hangzhou made the medal particularly meaningful.“Every event is very important. We believe that the Asian Games medal is the highest after the Olympics. I think this medal is shining amidst all the medals. The colour has changed. This medal means a lot to me,” Borgohain said.“I got a silver medal in the last Asian Games and this time I got a gold medal. This is why it is so special. And to do it on my birthday is extra special.”The victory also continued a curious connection between Borgohain and Japan. Five years ago, Tokyo had brought her an Olympic bronze medal — the breakthrough that changed the trajectory of her career.“I was very excited because I was going to Japan again. I had won a medal in (the) 2020 Olympics in Japan, and my life changed because of that,” she said.“I had a positive mindset before leaving India. I wanted to make it the best tournament of my life. I knew that I could do it because Japan is lucky for me.”The gold also offered a reminder of Borgohain’s ability to rebuild.Her career has not followed a straight line since the Tokyo Olympics. Injuries, changes in form and the disappointment of the Paris Olympics tested her, while the pressure that came with becoming an Olympic medallist added another layer to the challenge.Borgohain does not, however, see the Asian Games gold as something that has fundamentally changed her.“I don’t think I am looking at myself differently because of this medal. I have won and lost a lot of medals. People’s perspective changes because of the medal. But I am always the same in my own eyes,” she said.“My perspective has not changed because of the medal. When I lose, my self-belief remains the same. Sometimes I am confident, and sometimes I am down. But I am the same person that I was before.”That mindset became particularly important after Paris 2024, when she failed to reach the medal rounds. Borgohain describes the period as one of the most difficult phases of her career.“I have a 15-year journey. Every time I go to a competition, my mindset is different. When we play, we reach the medal. It is not easy to recover from a tough period. The 2024 Paris Olympics wasn’t an easy period for me mentally,” she said.“But I think everything is a game of the mind. It depends on how we look at it. If we take tough things easy, it becomes easy. If we take easy things hard, it becomes hard. I think that helped me a lot to keep myself calm and relaxed.”The Asian Games victory has also given Borgohain a more direct route towards the next stage of her career. The gold means she qualifies for the World Championships, rather than having to go through the national selection route. A strong performance there could also put her on the road to another Olympic qualification campaign.“It matters a lot for an athlete because of this medal I am qualifying for the World Championships. I am getting a good treat otherwise I would have to play the Nationals and follow the same process,” she said.“So that is a big advantage of the medal, and it boosts my confidence that I can do better. If I do well there, then I can qualify for the Olympics also.”For now, though, Borgohain is resisting the temptation to look too far ahead.“There is a lot of planning. But not everything is the same. I am living in the present. I don’t know what will happen tomorrow. I will try to live like this. It makes me feel good. I will try to live like this.”Borgohain’s gold was part of a strong boxing campaign for India at the Asian Games. India finished the competition with six boxing medals, including three golds, with Parveen Hooda and Ankush Panghal also winning their respective finals.Some months back, Indian boxers had returned with 10 medals at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, including seven golds. No country had won more golds in boxing at a single edition of the CWG. It was also India's largest haul in the sport in a CWG.For Borgohain, the improvement reflects a broader change in the mentality of Indian boxers.“We had a very good performance. Both men and women did very well. Everyone knows the results of the Commonwealth Games. The results of the Commonwealth Games changed the results of Indian Boxing,” she said.“In the Asian Games, our Indian team came out on top. I think our athletes are very strong. Their mentality is very good. We used to think that we would not be able to do it. But now our young athletes have the mindset that ‘we have to do it’.”She also pointed to the support structure around the team, including government backing and the environment created by the coaching staff led by Santiago Nieva.“The support of the government matters a lot. They don’t let us down. We are getting good competition. The environment of our foreign coaches, led by Santiago (Nieva), is very positive. That is why we are getting good results.”For Borgohain, then, the Asian Games gold is both an ending and a beginning — the end of a 12-year wait since Mary Kom’s historic gold and the completion of a personal journey from Hangzhou silver to Nagoya gold.But she is not treating it as a destination. The next target can wait. For now, she is content to live in the moment — with the gold medal still in her hand.
Article Summary: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain won gold at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. She beat China's Bao Ziyi 5-0 in the women's 75kg final. The victory, on her 29th birthday, made her only the second Indian woman after Mary Kom to win boxing gold.

Article Title: 'No one treats a human being like that': Ravi Shastri calls out Pakistan's treatment of jailed Imran Khan

Former India head coach Ravi Shastri has spoken out over the reported treatment of jailed former Pakistan captain Imran Khan , calling it “inhumane” and saying no person should be treated that way.Reports cited in the story claim Khan’s health has worsened in jail, with only 15% vision remaining in his right eye.Speaking to Republic World, Shastri said he was shocked by Khan’s situation and believed cricketers around the world would share his concerns."I'm not a politician. But just to see the way he's being treated today is shocking. You know, no one treats a human being like that. On humanitarian grounds, I don't think he deserves what he's getting. So I don't speak just for myself. I think there'll be a lot of cricketers around the globe who will be echoing the same sentiments," said Shastri.He also wished Khan good health and praised his achievements as a cricketer and captain, particularly his ability to guide young players."I just hope he's well and his health is good. Because what he gave to the game was something special. And my memories of him are just being an outstanding leader. You know, just a leader of men. The ability to motivate youngsters and then take them through. You said he came close at the age of 40, captain of the side, and he won the World Cup with a pretty young team," he added.Shastri said Khan, who has been in jail since 2023, is one of Pakistan’s most recognisable figures worldwide and should receive better treatment."Hopefully. Hope he comes out and is treated better. He's been there for a long time. You could be out somewhere else, in the same position, because I don't understand the politics. But to sit in a cell there, he doesn't deserve it because he's the most recognised Pakistani face globally.Whether you like it or not, that's my view," said Shastri.He also remembered Khan as a great all-rounder and leader, saying the India-Pakistan rivalry was built on mutual respect."This man you're seeing there with me was an unbelievable cricketer. I mean, a great cricketer is an understatement. The rivalry was out of respect."
Article Summary: Former India head coach Ravi Shastri has spoken out over the reported treatment of jailed former Pakistan captain Imran Khan. Reports claim Khan’s health has worsened in jail, with only 15% vision remaining in his right eye. He said he was shocked by Khan's situation and believed cricketers around the world would share his concerns.

Article Title: “Do we need Bad Boys t shirts this season?”: Dillon Brooks and John Collins’ massive preseason match fight puts NBA fans in a frenzy
Article Text:
Dillon Brooks and John Collins. Image via: Lon Horwedel / Imagn Images | NBA

Dillon Brooks and John Collins clash early in preseason opener

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NBA fans react to Brooks and Collins scuffle

Dillon Brooks and John Collins needed less than five minutes of Monday night's preseason opener between the Suns and Pistons to put hands on each other. A hard foul on an offensive rebound set it off, and players from both teams stepped in to pull them apart.The penalties were small, but the clip spread quickly, and the reaction split between laughter and disbelief. The Suns forward has a reputation for getting under opponents' skin, and the Pistons forward is the latest to get pulled in. Fans were soon asking whether Detroit needs Bad Boys T-shirts this season.The scrum started with 7:23 left in the first quarter. Collins had pulled down an offensive rebound and looked ready to score when he got hit with a hard foul. After the whistle, the Pistons forward grabbed Brooks by the throat and later pushed the ball into his face.Officials checked the replay and called a flagrant 1 on Collins and a technical on Brooks for unsportsmanlike contact. Lead official Karl Lane said Collins' actions were unnecessary. Phoenix shot two free throws, Detroit shot one, and play went on. ESPN's NBA account posted the clip with a note on the early intensity.It was the first exhibition game of the year for both clubs, played Oct. 5.There were no dirty plays, only small shots that piled up until both men went for the rebound. Many would agree that the throat grab was an overreaction for a preseason game.The clip went viral on the internet, and fans jumped into the comment sections of social media sites for their takes on the matter. Several fans were happy to see the intense drama during the game.@sharonljmoore put the question first: "Do we need Bad Boys t shirts this season?"@TheDreAboveAll went with a welcome: "Oh John Collins.. I was not familiar with this part of your game.. Welcome to Detroit. We'll get you settled in 💯"Timing got plenty of attention, since the game had barely started. @beasthazard92 wrote "Wasn't even 5 mins in 😂" and @PlayoffLucro added "NBA is really back chills 😂". @80sBearfan4life: "Wow this didn't take long and it's only in the preseason 😳"Brooks drew his own share. @Nox384 expects "he's gonna be a menace" this season. Others were less amused. @Rakememes: "This is basketball, not WWE 💀"@ilustriouseller: "grabbing a man neck like that is insane. There is a 6 whole months left in the season. How do you even escalate?"The Pistons secured the 109-107 win over the Suns, but the game will certainly be remembered by the fans and the NBA world.
Article Summary: The Suns forward has a reputation for getting under opponents' skin. Collins had pulled down an offensive rebound and looked ready to score when he got hit with a hard foul. After the whistle, the Pistons forward grabbed Brooks by the throat and later pushed the ball into his face. The Pistons secured the 109-107 win over the Suns.

Article Title: Major triple-threat title match set for WWE Money in the Bank 2026
Article Text:

WWE Money in the Bank 2026 will feature a major Women's title match

WWE Money in the Bank 2026 Premium Live Event is just days away, and a huge showdown has been made official. It will feature three competitors from the women's division battling it out in a high-stakes match, and only one will leave as the new champion.The October 5 episode of Monday Night RAW featured a blockbuster main event match between Becky Lynch and Liv Morgan. The match was to determine the No.1 contender to Stephanie Vaquer's WWE Women's World Championship at Money in the Bank 2026. This came off the heels of a feud brewing between the three women ever since Vaquer and Lynch returned to WWE on RAW after SummerSlam, after their respective hiatuses.The match was nothing short of heated, with tensions between Morgan and Lynch, who are longtime rivals themselves. Both women came hitting with their best moves from their respective arsenals. Yet neither was ready to give up that easily, with a huge title opportunity at stake. Overall, it was a highly exhilarating bout worthy of the main event of Monday Night RAW. However, the interesting turn came towards the end of the bout.Stephanie Vaquer came out to neutralize the threat of Morgan's allies, the Judgment Day, and then stood on the apron.This saw Becky Lynch accidentally take out Vaquer. Following that, Morgan attacked Vaquer and then turned her focus on Lynch. As they continued to trade blows, La Primera came back in the ring and attacked them both at the same time, ending the match in a double DQ. She then inflicted a major beatdown on both competitors, leading to the arrival of RAW GM Adam Pearce to control the situation.In a surprising turn of events, Vaquer demanded to face both Morgan and Lynch with her Women's World title on the line. The crowd came unglued, and Pearce made it official for Money in the Bank 2026. While it is commendable for Stephanie Vaquer to take on a tough challenge for her title, her chances of retaining it are slim now. So we will have to wait and see whether she can walk out of Money in the Bank with the gold still strapped around her waist.Also read: What does Naomi’s rumored WWE return mean for The Bloodline and its battle with The 946

NEW DELHI: A woman protester allegedly snatched the keys of a police bus carrying detained protesters during a demonstration in Delhi, preventing the vehicle from moving.A video of the incident has surfaced on social media.The incident took place amid protests in the national capital demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Heavy police deployment was witnessed at the protest sites, with several demonstrators detained during the agitation.In the viral video, the woman approached a police bus that was preparing to leave with detained protesters and managed to snatch its keys. She then ran away with them, leaving the bus stranded and unable to move.The incident quickly drew attention on social media, with users divided over the protester's action.While some praised her for preventing the vehicle carrying detained protesters from leaving, others questioned whether taking the keys of a police vehicle could lead to legal action.The authenticity of the video could not be independently verified by TOI.Meanwhile, All India Students' Association (AISA) national president Neha Bora was detained by Delhi Police on Sunday while leading a protest march towards Jantar Mantar.The march, which began near Andhra Bhawan Circle on Ashoka Road, was part of the third consecutive day of demonstrations by students and youth demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.AISA members and supporters raised slogans against the Election Commission as they attempted to move towards Jantar Mantar despite heavy barricading and security deployment.Police stopped the protesters as they approached the designated protest site and detained several demonstrators, including Bora.The protests came amid heightened security in central Delhi, with police deploying personnel and barricades to prevent protesters from moving beyond designated areas.
Article Summary: A woman protester allegedly snatched the keys of a police bus carrying detained protesters during a demonstration in Delhi. She then ran away with them, leaving the bus stranded and unable to move. The incident took place amid protests in the national capital demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Article Title: 'Captaincy ends': Harmanpreet Kaur’s top five achievements as India captain
Article Text:

1. Leading India to its maiden Women’s ODI World Cup title

Harmanpreet Kaur with World Cup title

2. Leading India to back-to-back Asian Games gold medals

Nagoya: India's captain Harmanpreet Kaur, right, and Gunalan Kamalini pose for photographs with Gold medals after winning the women's final T20I cricket match between India and Sri Lanka in the ongoing Asian Games 2026, in Nagoya, Japan. (PTI Photo/Arun Sharma)

3. Winning four Asia Cup titles

5. Leading India to a historic Test victory at Lord’s

A legacy that goes beyond the numbers
